files.role: Handwritten Operation equality and config/metadata overlap predicates, with two local unit tests. Public methods are reachable on the reexported Operation; conflicts is a private module.
ranges: SPDX/module docs say operation equality identifies the same retried change and metadata checks identify touched keys. Imports Operation/UpdateMap and HashSet. This file contains local equality and two public overlap predicates, not the full operation-pair conflict/rebase matrix. A contextual actual commit-outcome check compares durable protobuf transactions instead of in-memory Operation equality (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:246-283); do not infer its identity rule from this module comment.

Handwritten PartialEq::eq borrows self/other and defines nested compare_vec<T:PartialEq>: equal lengths AND every left element appears somewhere in right. Append compares fragment vectors through it. Order is ignored but multiplicities are not matched: distinct A,B give [A,A]==[A,B] in one direction only. Complexity is quadratic in vector lengths times element equality; no explicit allocation in this helper. TODO proposes sorted construction but is not implemented. Nested Fragment/other equality can have additional costs.

Clone/Clone compares all five payload fields directly: is_shallow,ref_name,ref_version,ref_path,branch_name. No URI/path canonicalization, case folding, version lookup or shallow-only validation; optional None and Some(empty) differ.

Delete/Delete applies compare_vec separately to updated_fragments and deleted_fragment_ids, then exact predicate string equality. Semantically equivalent SQL strings need not compare equal; fragment/ID vector ordering is ignored with the helper duplicate caveat.

Overwrite/Overwrite compares fragments with compare_vec, Schema directly, optional config HashMaps directly, and optional initial_bases Vec directly. Thus base order remains significant here, unlike UpdateBases later; None differs from Some(empty). No normalized-effect comparison or initial-ID ignoring occurs in equality even though overwrite construction docs describe final ID reassignment.

CreateIndex/CreateIndex compares new_indices and removed_indices independently with compare_vec, delegating complete IndexMetadata PartialEq to each entry rather than comparing only names/UUIDs. Order-insensitivity has the same duplicate caveat.

Rewrite/Rewrite compares groups and rewritten_indices with compare_vec, then directly compares optional frag_reuse_index, including its metadata contents. Group element equality itself uses an unordered-membership helper; RewrittenIndex equality includes details/version/optional files. In-memory reuse entry participates even though operation docs say it is not serialized (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:89-111; rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:363-397). Do not use this equality as a proved durable identity check.

Merge/Merge compares fragments with compare_vec, Schema directly and preserves_nullability bool directly. Equal schemas/fragments with different assertion flags are unequal. Neither validates the assertion nor checks row alignment.
Restore equality compares version u64 only; ReserveFragments compares num_fragments u32 only. No side effects or manifest lookup. Cross-kind cases are handled separately and always unequal.

Update/Update covers every current payload: compare_vec for removed IDs,updated fragments,new fragments,modified fields,compacted SSTables,preservation fields; direct equality for optional mode,inserted filter and updated offsets. HashMap/bitmap offsets use their structural equality, and filter equality includes stored representation/config, not merely logical key set. All vectors retain multiplicity caveats; no comparison normalizes duplicate fields/fragments or ignores transient inputs. CompactedSsTable contextual declaration compares shard UUID plus generation (rust/lance-table/src/system_index/mem_wal.rs:94-99).
Project/Project compares Schema and preserves_nullability directly. Same resulting schema with different proof assertion is unequal; no schema transition analysis in this arm.

UpdateConfig/UpdateConfig directly compares optional config/table/schema UpdateMaps and field-ID HashMap. UpdateMap derives PartialEq over ordered entries and replace flag, so different entry order can compare unequal even when resulting maps match; None differs from Some(empty), and a replacement differs from an incremental equivalent. Field HashMap iteration order itself is not meaningful for map equality (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/update_map.rs:13-56).

DataReplacement/DataReplacement repeats equal-length plus every-left-contained directly instead of calling compare_vec. Tuple equality compares fragment ID and DataFile. Comments introduce explicit cross-kind enumeration to force handling new variants; equality is not conflict compatibility.

Explicit Append-left cross-kind arms against Delete, Overwrite, CreateIndex, Rewrite, Merge, Restore, ReserveFragments, Update, Project, UpdateConfig, DataReplacement, UpdateMemWalState, Clone each compare std::mem::discriminant(self) with other. These are distinct variants, so every listed arm returns false independently of payload. No metadata-overlap or commit compatibility decision is made. Later UpdateBases and DataOverlay arms complete those pairs; blank separators carry no runtime behavior.

UpdateMemWalState/UpdateMemWalState compares compacted_sstables using compare_vec. Order is ignored, count must match and duplicate multiplicities remain unchecked; each table pointer equality includes shard UUID/generation.

Clone-left cross-kind arms against Append,Delete,Overwrite,CreateIndex,Rewrite,Merge,Restore,ReserveFragments,Update,Project,UpdateConfig,DataReplacement,UpdateMemWalState all compare differing discriminants and return false. UpdateBases/DataOverlay are handled below. These branches do not restrict legal shallow/deep clone operations.

UpdateBases/UpdateBases uses compare_vec for new_bases, unlike Overwrite.initial_bases direct Vec equality. Same elements in a different order can compare equal here; duplicates have membership asymmetry and no base-ID uniqueness check.

UpdateBases-left arms versus all14 other non-overlay variants (Append,Delete,Overwrite,CreateIndex,Rewrite,Merge,Restore,ReserveFragments,Update,Project,UpdateConfig,DataReplacement,UpdateMemWalState,Clone) compare discriminants and return false. No path/base merge or validation occurs.

Reverse arms put each of those14 non-overlay variants on left and UpdateBases on right, likewise returning false via differing discriminants. Both ordered comparisons are explicitly covered; this is enum inequality, not an assertion about whether transactions can coexist.

DataOverlay/DataOverlay uses compare_vec for groups. Each DataOverlayGroup derives equality over fragment ID plus ordered overlay Vec, so only outer group order is ignored; inner overlay order and committed versions remain meaningful. Remaining pairs with DataOverlay on either side return false, completing the16x16 variant cases. No tests here prove duplicate/reflexivity properties for arbitrary publicly constructed values (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/operation.rs:26-35).

Private Operation::get_upsert_config_keys returns owned Vec<String>. Overwrite Some(config_upsert_values) clones HashMap keys in unspecified order; UpdateConfig Some(config_updates) clones each Some-valued entry key in input order, preserving duplicates; other cases return empty. It ignores replace, final key effects, prior later deletes and all table/schema/field metadata. A Some(empty-string value) still counts as upsert.

Private get_delete_config_keys emits cloned None-valued entry keys only for UpdateConfig Some(config_updates), in list order with duplicates. All other variants including Overwrite return empty. replace=true does not add implicitly cleared keys and None entries still count as deletes even though apply_update_map replacement skips them. This is a syntactic intent extractor, not a final-map diff (rust/lance-table/src/transaction/update_map.rs:58-81).

Public modifies_same_metadata only handles two UpdateConfig variants. First table-map overlap uses update_maps_conflict; then any pair of Some schema_metadata_updates conflicts even if empty/disjoint; then any common field ID conflicts regardless of that field's inner keys or empty maps. Returns false if no category overlaps or either operation is another variant. Config updates are deliberately absent from this predicate and need upsert_key_conflict separately. No schema values, actual metadata contents, Merge or Overwrite special handling here.

Private update_maps_conflict returns false if either Option absent. With both Some, any replace=true returns true, even with zero entries on one or both sides. Otherwise collect left borrowed key strings into HashSet (duplicates collapse) and test any right key; insert versus delete values are ignored, so delete/delete same table key conflicts. Empty incremental map is disjoint. Expected linear hash work and O(unique left keys) additional references/storage; borrowed strings are not cloned.

Public upsert_key_conflict allocates four cloned-key Vecs from both operations, then checks left upserts intersect right upserts/deletes OR right upserts intersect left upserts/deletes. Shared delete-only keys are allowed; equal values still conflict; any syntactic upsert followed by deletion is still represented in both lists. replace flags/implicitly deleted keys are not considered. Vec::contains gives quadratic worst-case comparisons plus string costs; short-circuit occurs after all four lists have been built. Predicate is symmetric for ordinary strings. It returns bool with no error, IO, locks or mutation; consumer classifies the conflict.

cfg(test) imports parent plus shared overlay fixture, DataOverlayGroup/UpdateMapEntry and HashMap. Private table_metadata_update constructs UpdateConfig with Some table UpdateMap from borrowed tuple entries, supplied replace, and no config/schema/field edits. Uses public From conversion to own strings; it commits nothing.

Table metadata test compares one incremental upsert key=1 with same-key value2 (true), different-key value2 (false), and replacement of different key (true). It tests one argument order only; no missing options, empty maps, deletion pairs, schema/field categories, duplicate entries or config upsert predicate in this local test.

DataOverlay equality test uses local closure creating one group fragment0 with one legacy-file fixture field and committed_version1. Requires same field equality, differing field inequality, and inequality against empty Rewrite in overlay-left order. Comments refer to prior regressions but no historical commit is independently inspected. No outer-group permutation/duplicate, inner-order, reverse-kind, all-variant, config conflict or durable equality fixture here. Tests read, not executed.
files.limits: All1042 lines fully read in four bounded chunks. The256 ordered variant-kind equality cases are distinguished from commit compatibility. Full conflict_resolver.rs and durable protobuf encoder remain pending; narrow consumer context is recorded separately. No source edits, builds/tests or runtime reproduction. Contextual commit outcome compares protobuf forms (rust/lance/src/io/commit.rs:246-283), while shown overwrite/config consumer methods map predicates to conflicts (rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:1536-1583; rust/lance/src/io/commit/conflict_resolver.rs:2012-2072). Earlier checks in that resolver may impose additional rules.
